User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to create an academic-calendar draft for my campus and academic year so that I can configure the authoritative planning calendar.
Acceptance_Criteria: Gateway authenticates and applies tenant/institution/campus/year scope; required name, calendarCode, timezone and year are validated; DRAFT is created once per idempotency key; response contains calendarId, version, requestId and correlationId.
Events_and_Dependencies: Document-defined REST + IAM/RBAC/ABAC; AcademicCalendarCreated via outbox

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want duplicate calendar creation to be prevented so that each calendar code remains unique within its institutional scope.
Acceptance_Criteria: Enforce tenantId+institutionId+campusId+academicYear+calendarCode uniqueness; return conflict on duplicate; same idempotency key/replay returns original result; changed payload is rejected.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve a calendar by ID so that I can review its configuration and lifecycle state.
Acceptance_Criteria: Return authorized calendar metadata, status, currentVersion, effective boundaries and policy configuration; deny cross-scope access.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to update a draft calendar so that I can complete its configuration before submission.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only editable lifecycle states may be changed; updatedBy/updatedAt are captured; optimistic version checking prevents lost updates; published versions cannot be edited.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to cancel or deactivate an unsubmitted draft so that obsolete drafts are not accidentally processed.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only permitted draft states can be cancelled; transition is audited; cancelled drafts cannot be submitted or published.

User_Story: As an authorized management user, I want to search and filter calendars so that I can review academic schedules efficiently.
Acceptance_Criteria: Support pagination, filtering, sorting and tenant/scope restrictions; indexed queries are used where applicable.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a term or semester to a draft calendar so that instructional periods are defined.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only scoped editors can add terms to DRAFT; termCode and sequenceNo are unique within calendar; dates are valid; instructional dates remain within term boundaries.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want term-date overlaps to be rejected so that the academic calendar is internally consistent.
Acceptance_Criteria: Check proposed terms against existing indexed terms; reject impermissible overlap with ACD_CALENDAR_TERM_OVERLAP 422; persist nothing on failure.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to update a term in a draft calendar so that academic-period changes can be managed before publication.
Acceptance_Criteria: Use optimistic version checking; validate boundaries and instructional dates; audit the change; published term versions remain immutable.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve term details so that I can inspect dates, sequence and lifecycle state.
Acceptance_Criteria: Return term, calendar reference, dates, instructional dates, status and version within authorized scope.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to deactivate a draft term so that an obsolete term is not used in the calendar.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only non-published terms can be deactivated; change is recorded; references from draft events are validated.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to declare a holiday so that downstream planning reflects a non-working academic day.
Acceptance_Criteria: Validate HOLIDAY type, date boundary, eventCode and NON_WORKING impact; save against calendar; audit and reliably publish HolidayDeclared.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a working-day override so that special instructional or closure days are represented correctly.
Acceptance_Criteria: Validate WORKING_DAY_OVERRIDE and WORKING/NON_WORKING/NO_IMPACT; apply configured precedence; audit and version the change.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to schedule an academic event so that institutional activities are represented in the authoritative calendar.
Acceptance_Criteria: Validate type, title, dates, allDay, impact, optional termId and academic-year boundary; enforce unique eventCode; return eventId/version.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to list calendar events so that I can review events by date, type and term.
Acceptance_Criteria: Support date-range, type and term filtering with tenant/calendar scope enforcement and indexed access.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve an event by ID so that I can inspect its complete definition.
Acceptance_Criteria: Return eventCode, eventType, title, dates, allDay, workingDayImpact, category, status and version.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to update a draft event so that schedule changes can be incorporated before publication.
Acceptance_Criteria: Validate date/type/term rules; use optimistic version checking; audit change; reject edits to published event versions.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to deactivate a draft event so that obsolete events are not used.
Acceptance_Criteria: Use soft lifecycle transition for editable events; preserve published history; record audit entry.
Traceability: Architecture image API endpoint; immutable history

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to validate a draft before submission so that I can correct conflicts and missing configuration.
Acceptance_Criteria: Validate academic-year boundaries, term overlap, instructional containment, event conflicts, working-day precedence and publish prerequisites; return actionable errors without mutation.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want event dates outside the academic-year boundary to be rejected unless policy allows an exception.
Acceptance_Criteria: Reject invalid boundaries; permit only approved institutional-policy exceptions; return deterministic validation error.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want holiday and academic-event conflicts detected before publication so that the calendar is internally consistent.
Acceptance_Criteria: Identify conflicts using configured rules; block or classify them for review; do not silently modify source data.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want calendar impact analysis for proposed changes so that downstream effects can be understood before publication.
Acceptance_Criteria: Compare proposed version with current published version and classify affected dates/terms/events and downstream consumers; analysis is advisory.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to submit a validated calendar for approval so that it follows academic governance.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only validated DRAFT can transition to SUBMITTED; scope is checked; reason, requestId and correlationId are recorded; workflow reference is stored.

User_Story: As a Registrar, I want to approve or reject a submitted calendar so that only reviewed schedules can become effective.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only SUBMITTED calendars may be decided; Registrar authorization is enforced; decision/reason are append-only; rejected drafts cannot publish until permitted resubmission.

User_Story: As an Academic Admin, I want to resubmit a corrected rejected calendar so that it can re-enter the approval process.
Acceptance_Criteria: Only permitted rejected/correctable drafts may be resubmitted; new validation is required; history retains previous rejection reason and new submission.

User_Story: As a Registrar, I want to publish an approved calendar version so that one effective calendar is available for the campus.
Acceptance_Criteria: Validate approval context, expectedVersion and actor scope; ensure draft is complete; publish new version atomically.
MongoDB_Collections: academic_calendars; calendar_terms; calendar_events; calendar_history; outbox_events; idempotency_records
Events_and_Dependencies: Workflow approval; optimistic concurrency; MongoDB transaction; AcademicCalendarPublished

User_Story: As a Registrar, I want publication to supersede the previous current calendar atomically so that consumers never see two current versions.
Acceptance_Criteria: Transactionally mark previous current version SUPERSEDED, establish new PUBLISHED version, append history and create outbox records; concurrent race returns version conflict.

User_Story: As a Registrar, I want to create a new draft from a published calendar so that changes preserve the immutable published record.
Acceptance_Criteria: Clone required calendar/term/event state into a new editable version; preserve source version reference; classify impact before approval.

User_Story: As a System Administrator, I want published versions to be immutable so that historical academic decisions remain trustworthy.
Acceptance_Criteria: Published calendar/term/event records cannot be updated destructively; changes require a new draft/version; history remains append-only.

User_Story: As an authorized academic consumer, I want to retrieve the current effective calendar for a campus and academic year so that planning uses authoritative dates.
Acceptance_Criteria: Return the single current PUBLISHED calendar and relevant terms/events for authorized scope; no direct DB access.
Events_and_Dependencies: ACD-05; ACD-06; EXM; IAM service authorization

User_Story: As an Attendance service consumer, I want to resolve effective term and working-day status for a date so that attendance rules use the correct calendar context.
Acceptance_Criteria: Resolve effective calendar version by operating date, then apply term, holiday and working-day override precedence.

User_Story: As an authorized academic consumer, I want upcoming events and holidays in a date range so that dependent services can plan activities.
Acceptance_Criteria: Return effective events within requested range using indexed date queries and authorized scope.

User_Story: As a Registrar, I want to review immutable calendar history so that I can trace approvals, publications and supersessions.
Acceptance_Criteria: History is append-only and contains action, status transition, actor, timestamp, reason, correlationId and approvalRef where applicable.

User_Story: As a Compliance Officer, I want significant calendar and access actions audited so that governance and investigations have complete evidence.
Acceptance_Criteria: Audit create/edit/term/holiday/event/submission/approval/publication/supersession/export and authorization failures with actor, scope, old/new state, reason, requestId and correlationId.

User_Story: As an Auditor, I want history queries filtered by calendar, actor and time so that investigations can be performed efficiently.
Acceptance_Criteria: Support calendarId+changedAt and changedBy+changedAt access patterns while respecting governance permissions.

User_Story: As a Security Administrator, I want API Gateway authentication and trusted identity propagation so that only authenticated callers reach ACD-07.
Acceptance_Criteria: Gateway authenticates caller, validates credential/token according to platform IAM, propagates trusted tenant/user context and rejects unauthenticated traffic.

User_Story: As a Security Administrator, I want RBAC and ABAC enforced so that calendar actions are restricted by role and academic scope.
Acceptance_Criteria: Academic Admin can create/edit/submit in scope; Registrar can approve/publish/supersede; Management has authorized read; tenant/institution/campus/year predicates are enforced.

User_Story: As a Platform Administrator, I want rate limiting at the API Gateway so that excessive traffic cannot degrade ACD-07.
Acceptance_Criteria: Apply configured consumer/tenant/scope limits; return HTTP 429 on excess traffic; rejected requests do not modify ACD-07 MongoDB; throttling metrics are available.

User_Story: As a Security Administrator, I want tenant isolation enforced on every API and query so that one organization cannot access another organization's calendars.
Acceptance_Criteria: tenantId is mandatory for business records; ABAC restricts tenant/institution/campus/year; cross-tenant reads and writes are denied.

User_Story: As an API client, I want standardized pagination, filtering, sorting and error envelopes so that all ACD-07 APIs behave consistently.
Acceptance_Criteria: All list APIs support standard pagination/filtering/sorting; domain errors map to documented HTTP status codes and codes.

User_Story: As an API client, I want retryable calendar writes to be idempotent so that network retries do not create duplicate data or publications.
Acceptance_Criteria: Create/publish accepts Idempotency-Key; same key+same request returns stored outcome; same key+different hash is rejected; TTL applies where configured.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want calendar-domain events stored in an outbox with the business update so that downstream consumers receive reliable notifications.
Acceptance_Criteria: Business state and outbox event commit atomically where practical; eventId is unique; payload/status/retry metadata are stored.

User_Story: As a downstream consumer, I want canonical ACD-07 events so that I can reliably react to calendar changes.
Acceptance_Criteria: Published events include eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, entityType, entityId, version, correlationId and data.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want transient event-delivery failures retried so that temporary broker failures do not lose calendar notifications.
Acceptance_Criteria: Retry transient failures using attemptCount/nextAttemptAt; retain delivery state until successful publication.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want poison events isolated in a dead-letter store so that repeated failures do not block healthy events.
Acceptance_Criteria: After bounded retries, store event payload/failure reason/attempt count in dead_letter_events; support controlled replay and investigation.

User_Story: As an event consumer, I want duplicate events deduplicated by eventId so that retries do not cause duplicate downstream processing.
Acceptance_Criteria: Consumer checks eventId, safely ignores already processed events, and retains correlation/causation identifiers.

User_Story: As the Academic Calendar Service, I want to consume CampusUpdated events so that calendar scope remains aligned with campus configuration.
Acceptance_Criteria: Deduplicate by eventId; validate/refresh referenced campus context without owning campus data; failures are observable and handled through retry/DLQ.

User_Story: As the Academic Calendar Service, I want to consume InstitutionConfigurationChanged events so that calendar policies remain current.
Acceptance_Criteria: Refresh/validate applicable working-day and publication policies; deduplicate; route failed processing through bounded retry/DLQ.

User_Story: As a downstream academic service, I want calendar changes distributed through APIs/events rather than database access so that ACD-07 remains the owner of calendar truth.
Acceptance_Criteria: Consumers use stable calendarId/version/effective dates and event contracts; no downstream service can query academic_calendar_db directly.
Events_and_Dependencies: ACD-05; ACD-06; EXM; CAM; LMS; Analytics

User_Story: As a Management User, I want monthly, weekly, department and program-oriented calendar views so that I can review academic schedules.
Acceptance_Criteria: Views derive from authoritative effective calendar; access is scoped; large report generation can run asynchronously.

User_Story: As a Management User, I want to export an authorized calendar to PDF, Excel or ICS so that schedule information can be shared through approved channels.
Acceptance_Criteria: Export reflects effective or explicitly selected version; permissions are enforced; export is audited; large exports may be asynchronous.

User_Story: As a Management User, I want advisory calendar analytics so that I can identify instructional-day density, holiday concentration, term anomalies and change impact.
Acceptance_Criteria: Analytics are derived from calendar data; insights are advisory only and cannot silently modify authoritative calendar state.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want current-calendar and date-range queries to use the defined MongoDB indexes so that ACD-07 meets its performance targets.
Acceptance_Criteria: Verify indexes for current calendars, term dates, event dates/types and history; normal API P95 target <300ms and indexed search P95 <2s.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want ACD-07 to scale statelessly so that increasing campus/tenant load does not require service redesign.
Acceptance_Criteria: Service pods remain stateless; indexes are tenant-aware; stable current-calendar reads may be safely cached; event streams can partition by tenant/institution.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want correlated logs, metrics and traces so that calendar workflow failures and delivery lag are diagnosable.
Acceptance_Criteria: requestId/correlationId flow through API, persistence and event envelope; dashboards track API latency/errors, validation failures, publication latency, outbox lag, delivery failures, current-calendar count and upcoming events.

User_Story: As an API client, I want consistent ACD-07 domain errors so that I can handle failures safely.
Acceptance_Criteria: Duplicate current=409; term overlap=422; invalid date=422; publish forbidden=403; version conflict=409; not found=404; dependency unavailable=503; deterministic validation failures are not retried.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want mandatory dependency failures to fail closed where policy validation is required so that invalid calendars are not published during dependency outages.
Acceptance_Criteria: Required configuration/workflow/authorization dependencies produce controlled 503/failure; no unsafe publication occurs; failures are observable.

User_Story: As a System Administrator, I want retention policies applied to business and technical collections so that required records are preserved without uncontrolled technical growth.
Acceptance_Criteria: Calendar history follows institutional retention; outbox retained through safe delivery plus safety window; DLQ through incident/audit period; idempotency records may use TTL.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want backup and restore verification so that recovery does not violate calendar integrity.
Acceptance_Criteria: Encrypted backups/PITR where available; restore preserves versions/history and required outbox recovery; post-restore verification confirms exactly one current published calendar per required scope.

User_Story: As a System Administrator, I want MongoDB JSON Schema and application validation enforced so that invalid records cannot bypass domain rules.
Acceptance_Criteria: Schemas validate required fields/types; compound unique indexes enforce business keys; reference and lifecycle validation occurs in application/domain layer; direct cross-service DB writes are prohibited.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want optimistic concurrency controls on calendar changes so that simultaneous administrators cannot silently overwrite each other.
Acceptance_Criteria: Version fields are checked on updates/publication; stale expectedVersion produces ACD_CALENDAR_VERSION_CONFLICT 409; no partial state is committed.

User_Story: As a Development Team, I want approved OpenAPI, JSON Schema and event contracts for ACD-07 so that implementations and consumers remain compatible.
Acceptance_Criteria: OpenAPI covers REST surface; JSON schemas validate MongoDB documents; event contracts are registered; contract tests cover REST and Event Bus compatibility.
Traceability: Production Definition of Done; testing strategy

User_Story: As a Development Team, I want automated tests for ACD-07 business and resilience rules so that releases do not break calendar integrity.
Acceptance_Criteria: Unit tests cover dates/overlaps/lifecycle; integration tests cover MongoDB/workflow/config adapters; security tests cover RBAC/ABAC/tenant isolation; resilience tests cover DB/broker/dependency failures; E2E covers draft-to-consumer flow.

User_Story: As a Platform Operator, I want the ACD-07 production Definition of Done enforced so that the service is operationally ready.
Acceptance_Criteria: OpenAPI approved; validators/indexes verified; publication transaction tested; outbox/idempotency/DLQ operational; workflow/RBAC reviewed; audit, dashboards, alerts, tracing, backup/restore and event contracts verified; tenant isolation passed.
